original_card.question: Can one small, precisely scoped interface lemma be formalized with its actual hypotheses?
methods: Formalize a missing boundary lemma identified by the selected review.
Audit a formal theorem-to-certificate binding independently.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State the exact formalized proposition and remaining assumptions; avoid duplicate arithmetic formalizations already present.

first_step.inspect: Read the exact hypotheses in the hyperplane-end proof and distinguish Lean theorems from finite supplier assumptions.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: State one missing boundary lemma in full before starting a proof-assistant build.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A missing interface proof can reduce the conditional gap even if it does not change kappa.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one formal lemma or one theorem-to-certificate binding.
scope_change_triggers: Formalizing already-covered arithmetic and claiming the full multiplication theorem.

actual_scope: Separately authored audit of PR1624 (head 712a9b9aa8802d0135a578c0debee7b56c8e492f, an664 / Andrey Mas): the fixed PR1020 26-puncture, designated pair (48, 0), eight-term separate-COPY minimum 62. Recompute every finite premise of proof.md Sections 2, 4-6, 8 and 9 from its prose spec without reading PR1624's programs, audit the written Section 3/7/9 argument, and bind the charge model to merged PR1020's own executed cost code.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a formal lemma or a theorem-to-certificate binding; PR1624 is a written theorem whose two checkers came from one session and whose 69-cost baseline was replayed from transcribed data. A separately authored check of its finite premises and a predecessor-code binding is the missing independent evidence for that theorem. No proof assistant is used.
bottleneck_link: Side result: independent verification of a pending scoped algebraic checkpoint on the complex masked-decoder line. It changes no kappa and prices no physical decoder; it lets a reviewer accept or reject PR1624's fixed-object minimum without trusting single-session agreement.
stop_rule: Stop after the finite premises, the written audit and the PR1020 binding; do not extend to other punctures or pairs.
evidence: verify.py: all finite premises reproduced exactly (label basis, 14,400-entry bilinear identity, minor -256, 511 kernels = 482 rank-8 + 29 rank-7 on 27 lines P u {30}, full Section 5 table, 13 a-perp / 1 b-perp candidates, c dots, 62 witness on 8,836 entries with Section 8 table, 256 seven-sets = structural formula, all 256 classes expanded entrywise at cost 62, own branch-67 witness, section 10 complex example over Q(i) at 63 with the real look-alike's supports checked equal); PR1020's own decoder_check prices its decoder at 69 and PR1624's witness at 62. Written audit in README finds no gap in Sections 3, 7 and 9.
